fields.title: This is the remote server
fields.help_text: Check this on the live/target site of a sync pair. It disables this site's own sync cron job and the manual sync actions below (Check Now, Resync Now, Push to Remote) — this site is only ever the destination, never the one initiating checks. The "/rest-in-sync/v1/meta/{id}" REST route (used by the other site to fetch full meta data) keeps working regardless, since that's what makes this useful as a remote target in the first place.

fields.html: The settings below only matter for a site that initiates its own sync checks, so they're hidden while "This is the remote server" is checked.
Enter the connection details for the live WordPress site this plugin will sync to.

fields.title: Site URL
fields.help_text: The full URL of the live WordPress site, including https://.

fields.title: Username
fields.help_text: The username of a user on the live site with permission to manage content.

fields.title: Application Password
fields.help_text: Generate this under the live site's Users → Profile → Application Passwords.

fields.title: Post Types to Sync
fields.help_text: Choose which post types should be checked and validated via the REST API.

fields.html: The sync status cron job periodically compares local posts against the remote site and flags any that have drifted out of sync.

fields.title: Cron Batch Size
fields.help_text: How many posts to check for changes on each cron run.

fields.title: Sync Check Interval
fields.help_text: How often the cron job runs to check posts for out-of-sync changes.

fields.title: Resync Threshold (hours)
fields.help_text: Posts checked more recently than this many hours ago are skipped until this many hours have passed. Posts that have never been checked are always processed.
